(arXiv 2406.09289) on the\nout-of-distribution brittleness of steering vectors, these are why the iteration-1 claim that a perturbation\ncloses the rank-one forgery route was withdrawn: 0.803 is a usable direction, and an adversary who knows the\nmetric's definition refits on the metric's own distribution at identical cost. The perturbation arm survives as\na measurement run in Stage 0, and the rank-one rung is closed by the weight instrument instead. All score\nPROMPTS with a fixed model; none produces a per-checkpoint number.\"\"\",\n    \"\"\"arXiv 2406.05946, 'Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep', established that\nalignment is often shallow and that deepening it is a training objective. It diagnoses shallowness WITH training\naccess and then fixes it. We ask the question it leaves untouched: can shallowness be read off a single\ndownloaded checkpoint with no reference and no training access, and does that reading predict how much safety\nsurvives a shift. arXiv 2412.09565, 'Obfuscated Activations Bypass LLM Latent-Space Defenses', is the closest\nwork on gaming an internal readout and reports an obfuscation tax, but its object is a per-input monitor at\ninference time defended by a probe the attacker can query, and its direction is making a harmful input look\nbenign; ours is a model-level certificate computed by a downloader who never meets the uploader, making an\nunsafe MODEL look safe through levers a monitor-evasion attacker does not have, starting with the repository's\nown configuration files.\"\"\",\n    \"\"\"arXiv 2602.04653, on inference-time backdoors via chat templates, with its static scan of roughly 192,000 Hub\nchat templates, establishes that the files shipping beside the weights are an unexamined and widely exploitable\nsurface. It points that lever at making models behave badly; we point the identical zero-cost lever at making\nmodels SCORE well. Because a content scan of the shipped template is reference-free, our rung zero is metric\nhygiene rather than a threat, so it is reported and then removed from the headline, which starts one rung up.\narXiv 2505.17815 and arXiv 2509.18058 establish that evaluations can be defeated from the inside by a model that\ninfers it is being tested; they locate the agency in the MODEL, we locate it in the PUBLISHER and in files the\nmodel never sees as input, and the two failure modes call for opposite defences.\"\"\",\n    \"\"\"Efficient-benchmarking work using item response theory is the one place the two sides of safety are combined.\narXiv 2608.05086, 'Item Response Theory for AI Safety', makes the adaptive-item claim that roughly ten adaptively\nchosen items suffice for several individual benchmarks, cutting evaluation cost by 97 to 99 percent; arXiv\n2606.20626 reports a reduction of at least 80 percent. That line points harmful-refusal and over-refusal the same\nway by sign-flipping the over-refusal benchmark, but it is fully behavioural, needs the benchmark items, and\nyields a ranking factor rather than an operating point. No cheap metric read from weights or activations has been\nvalidated against a target a model refusing everything loses on.\"\"\",\n    \"\"\"arXiv 2502.16173, 'Mapping 1,000+ Language Models via the Log-Likelihood Vector' (ACL 2025), is the closest\nprecedent for the manifold limb: it gives every model coordinates whose squared Euclidean distance approximates\nthe divergence between generation distributions, and builds a map over more than a thousand models, which is the\nscale our honest-manifold fit needs and the evidence such a fit is affordable. Those coordinates are black-box\nand about similarity and lineage rather than safety, and nothing there asks whether a checkpoint sits off the\nmanifold because someone edited it. We adopt it as precedent AND as a baseline: if a log-likelihood model map\ndetects our forgeries as well as a metric-vector manifold does, the internal coordinates have not earned their\nforward passes, and we report that.\"\"\",\n    \"\"\"The secret-draw protocol is deliberately NOT claimed as novel and the literature is cited so it cannot be\nmistaken for a claim. Private and dynamic benchmarking - Dynabench (arXiv 2104.14337), Shirali, Abebe and Hardt's\n'A Theory of Dynamic Benchmarks' (arXiv 2210.03165), which proves iterated benchmark-versus-model fitting stalls\nafter about three rounds, and TRUCE private benchmarking (arXiv 2403.00393) - all do the same thing for the same\nreason, for black-box behavioural items. Strategic classification (arXiv 1506.06980) supplies the\ncost-of-manipulation vocabulary but assumes the scoring rule is public and fixed, where our hidden randomness is\nthe item draw rather than the rule. Casper, Ezell, Siegmann et al., 'Black-Box Access is Insufficient for Rigorous\nAI Audits' (FAccT 2024, arXiv 2401.14446), is the policy argument that audits must look inside the model, which\nour weight-and-activation instantiation is a concrete instance of. What none combines is a metric read from\nweights or activations, an adversary who knows the metric's definition but not the audit-time draw, and a\nperturbation-family pool as the source of that secrecy.\"\"\",\n]\n\nH[\"inspiration\"] = \"\"\"\nThe frame came from anti-doping laboratories, and so did both repairs. An athlete can raise a testosterone\nLEVEL, and for years the test was that level, so the test was beaten. What replaced it was the carbon isotope\nratio: synthetic testosterone carries a different carbon-13 signature, so the fraud is caught not by the size of\nany one number but by an inconsistency between numbers that a real body cannot produce apart. The same principle\nruns through forensic accounting, where fabricated books satisfy the headline total but violate the joint\ndistribution of leading digits, and through art authentication, where the pigment is right and the pigment's trace\nelements are wrong. Safety metrics for downloaded models are currently all levels, and nobody has asked what their\nratios do.\n\nAnti-doping also did not defeat targeted evasion by inventing an un-spikeable analyte. It used OUT-OF-COMPETITION\nRANDOM TESTING, so the athlete cannot know when or what is measured, and the ATHLETE BIOLOGICAL PASSPORT, which\ncatches the intervention by the trace it leaves rather than by the value it produces. Both transfer: the audit's\nitems are drawn at audit time rather than published, and the rank-one edit is closed by the trace it writes into\nevery layer it touches.\n\nThis iteration's repair came from a fourth field, and from taking a critique seriously rather than defending\nagainst it. The previous instrument measured the SIZE of a spectral anomaly, and sizes are exactly what differs\nbetween one trained network and another, so the honest baseline moved more than the signal did. Chemometrics and\nsignal processing solved that problem long ago by throwing the magnitudes away and keeping only the SUBSPACE - the\nprincipal angles between what two measurements span, which is what a Grassmannian distance is for. A projector\nknows which directions a matrix uses and nothing about how strongly. That single change makes the statistic\ninvariant to every layer's own spectrum, and it converts the reviewer's kill shot into a measurement: a per-layer\nabliteration tool is not drawing random directions, it is estimating the same refusal feature at every layer, so\nthe alignment it leaves is a number to be measured rather than an assumption to be defended.\n\nTwo further imports shaped the design. From economics, costly signalling: a signal is informative only when it is\nexpensive to produce for those lacking the underlying quality, which converts \"is this metric valid\" into the\nmeasurable \"what does forging it cost\". From clinical-trial statistics, the habit of asking whether a candidate\nmarker merely reports the outcome you can already see or predicts one you cannot - here the difference between\npredicting a benchmark score, which a plain refusal rate already does, and predicting whether that score survives a\nlineage or a condition the benchmark did not contain.\n\nThe last piece is internal: the field's own repeated negative result, that a plain refusal rate and even the model\ncard beat every internal readout. That is a strange result to accept at face value, and the resolution offered here\nis that behaviour will always win at predicting behaviour on honest models, so the comparison has to be run where\nbehaviour is not a reliable witness - on a lineage nobody tuned on, and on a checkpoint someone had a reason to\nshape.\n\"\"\".strip()\n\nH[\"terms\"] = [\n    {\"term\": \"Cheap safety metric\",\n     \"definition\": \"A number estimating how safe a model is, computed from a single checkpoint in seconds to a couple of minutes from its weights, a few dozen short forward passes, or a handful of generations, with no parent model, no attested base to diff against, and no benchmark run.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Level metric\",\n     \"definition\": \"A norm, rate, mean projection or unconditional propensity read at a fixed direction, layer and token position - a functional of the model evaluated without reference to how it varies across inputs. Predicted to be the constant-forgeable class and the class that fails on held-out lineages. A zero-prompt metric has no item axis, so it is a level by construction, which is why the floor on a trustworthy metric is not zero prompts.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Across-item metric\",\n     \"definition\": \"A correlation, rank ordering or area under a curve computed over the item set, and therefore invariant to a constant offset - exactly so for a linear read at the injection layer, and approximately for anything read through a normalisation, where the pre-registered tolerance is 0.05 correlation units.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Forgery cost\",\n     \"definition\": \"The cheapest rung of a fixed cost-ordered ladder of checkpoint edits that pushes a metric past a threshold set at a stated false-positive rate on a large honest panel, while the model's two-sided safety does not improve by more than a powered margin. Recorded in wall-clock seconds, training FLOPs and labelled examples, and reported as a curve over false-positive rates.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Detection cost, Tier A and Tier B\",\n     \"definition\": \"What it costs an auditor to notice a rung was applied. TIER A is reference-free and uses only the downloaded repository with no knowledge of its family: content checks on the chat template and generation config, a state-dict key-and-shape check against the architecture named in config.json, and the zero-prompt weight statistic. TIER B additionally diffs those files against the family default, which presumes an attested reference. Tier A is the headline because it is the access model the request specifies; the gap between the tiers measures how much detection power comes from knowing the family.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Undetectable forgery cost\",\n     \"definition\": \"The headline quantity: the cheapest rung that both pushes the metric into the safe region and survives the Tier A reference-free screen. It can be far higher than plain forgery cost for exactly the rungs that leave a structural trace, and if it turns out to be constant across the battery that is itself the result - the only undetectable forgery is training.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Forgery ladder\",\n     \"definition\": \"Six rungs. F0, an edit to files shipping in the repository. F1, an inference-time system prompt. F2a, the CONSTANT rung. F2b, the RANK-ONE rung. F3, a small keyword-triggered refusal adapter trained for about a hundred steps. F4, genuine light safety fine-tuning on real paired data, which buys real safety and caps the ladder.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Constant rung, F2a\",\n     \"definition\": \"An item-independent additive offset to a band of residual writes. As a change to the linear map this is rank zero, and the identical offset lands on every item so it cancels exactly from any across-item statistic read linearly at the injection layer. How it is BUILT matters for detection: most panel architectures define no bias on the attention output or MLP down projections, so an explicit bias tensor is caught for free by a key-and-shape check, and the offset is therefore realised instead on a near-constant carrier coordinate such as an attention-sink or massive-activation dimension, with its across-item constancy verified against the 0.05 tolerance.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Rank-one rung, F2b\",\n     \"definition\": \"The residual write becomes W x plus alpha r (d transpose x), which is item-dependent because each item is scaled by its own component along d. This is genuinely rank one in the map, it CAN move across-item statistics, and it is a published method rather than a trick invented here. It writes one shared direction into every write matrix it touches.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Abliteration\",\n     \"definition\": \"A training-free community edit that suppresses a refusal direction in the weights, replacing W by (I minus kappa r r transpose) W, producing an uncensored checkpoint. At kappa equal to one it is a projection, so it is singular and has no inverse. Because it removes each item's own component along r it is ITEM-DEPENDENT and belongs in the rank-one class, so its filed prediction is not invariance but a FALL in across-item coupling. Real recipes vary in three ways that matter to any weight detector: whether one direction is shared across layers or fitted per layer, whether kappa is one or less, and whether all layers or a band are edited.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Subspace alignment (the shared-direction scar)\",\n     \"definition\": \"The repaired zero-prompt, parent-free weight statistic, and the detection column's whole content. For each residual-write matrix, form the projector onto its bottom-k (or top-k) LEFT singular subspace; average those projectors over a contiguous band of layers; take the largest eigenvalue. Bottom-subspace alignment reads abliteration, top-subspace alignment reads injection. Because a projector discards singular values, the statistic is invariant to each layer's own spectrum, which is what the previous raw-Gram version was not. Because it is windowed, an edit confined to part of the stack is found rather than diluted. Because it is a continuous overlap, it degrades gracefully in the realised cross-layer cosine instead of knife-edging at the ideal recipe. It reads an EDIT rather than a RISK and is never reported as a safety score.\"},\n    {\"term\": \"Local rank deficiency\",\n     \"definition\": \"The companion statistic that needs no sharing at all: per matrix, the ratio of the smallest to the second-smallest singular value. A full-strength projection makes the matrix exactly rank-deficient and collapses this ratio, whatever direction each layer used and whatever that layer's spectrum looks like, so it catches per-layer abliteration which subspace alignment is blind to by construction. import numpy as np, time
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
d, n, L = 256, 1024, 28

def rand_orth(m,k,rg):
    Q,_ = np.linalg.qr(rg.standard_normal((m,k))); return Q[:,:k]

def make_W(kind, rg):
    U = rand_orth(d,d,rg); V = rand_orth(n,d,rg)
    if kind=='gauss':
        x = rg.standard_normal((d,n))/np.sqrt(n)
        s = np.sqrt(np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(x@x.T))[::-1])
    else:
        s = (np.arange(1,d+1)**-0.8)
    return U@np.diag(s)@V.T

def bf16(W):
    a = np.ascontiguousarray(W.astype(np.float32)).view(np.uint32)
    a = ((a.astype(np.uint64) + 0x8000) & 0xFFFF0000).astype(np.uint32)
    return a.view(np.float32).astype(np.float64)

def eig(W):                      # left spectrum + left singular vectors, via d x d Gram
    e,U = np.linalg.eigh(W@W.T)  # ascending
    return np.clip(e,0,None), U

def stats(Ws, k=1, win=8):
    E=[eig(W) for W in Ws]
    Pb=[U[:,:k]@U[:,:k].T for _,U in E]          # bottom-k left subspace
    Pt=[U[:,-k:]@U[:,-k:].T for _,U in E]        # top-k left subspace
    def align(P,w):
        best=0.0
        for st in range(0,len(P)-w+1):
            best=max(best,np.linalg.eigvalsh(np.mean(P[st:st+w],axis=0))[-1])
        return best
    botgap=min(np.sqrt(e[0]/e[1]) for e,_ in E)
    G=sum(W@W.T for W in Ws); g=np.linalg.eigvalsh(G)
    Gh=sum(d*(W@W.T)/np.trace(W@W.T) for W in Ws)/len(Ws); gh=np.linalg.eigvalsh(Gh)
    return dict(G_lmin=g[0]/g.mean(), G_lmax=g[-1]/g.mean(), nG_lmin=gh[0],
                BSA_all=align(Pb,len(Ws)), BSA_w=align(Pb,win),
                TSA_all=align(Pt,len(Ws)), TSA_w=align(Pt,win), botgap=botgap)

def abl(Ws, rl, kappa, frac):
    nl=int(round(frac*len(Ws)))
    return [ (np.eye(d)-kappa*np.outer(rl[i],rl[i]))@W if i<nl else W.copy()
             for i,W in enumerate(Ws) ]

def inject(Ws, rl, alpha):
    out=[]
    for i,W in enumerate(Ws):
        v=rng.standard_normal(n); v/=np.linalg.norm(v)
        out.append(W+alpha*np.sqrt(np.trace(W@W.T)/d)*np.outer(rl[i],v))
    return out

def dirs(mode, rho=None):
    r0=rng.standard_normal(d); r0/=np.linalg.norm(r0)
    if mode=='shared': return [r0]*L
    out=[]
    for _ in range(L):
        x=rng.standard_normal(d); x/=np.linalg.norm(x)
        y=x if mode=='perlayer' else rho*r0+np.sqrt(1-rho**2)*x
        out.append(y/np.linalg.norm(y))
    return out

def cos_of(rl):
    M=np.array(rl); C=np.abs(M@M.T); iu=np.triu_indices(len(rl),1); return C[iu].mean()

cols=['G_lmin','G_lmax','nG_lmin','BSA_all','BSA_w','TSA_w','botgap']
for spec in ['gauss','heavy']:
    print(f"\n===== honest spectrum = {spec}  (d={d}, fan-in={n}, L={L}, window=8) =====",flush=True)
    Ws=[make_W(spec,rng) for _ in range(L)]
    print(f"{'recipe':<30}{'xlayer_cos':>11}"+"".join(f"{c:>11}" for c in cols),flush=True)
    def rec(name,X,c=None):
        s=stats(X); cs='-' if c is None else f"{c:.3f}"
        print(f"{name:<30}{cs:>11}"+"".join(f"{s[c2]:>11.4g}" for c2 in cols),flush=True)
    rec('HONEST',Ws)
    rec('HONEST bf16',[bf16(W) for W in Ws])
    for kap in [1.0,0.7,0.5,0.3]:
        r=dirs('shared'); rec(f'ABL shared kappa={kap}',abl(Ws,r,kap,1.0),cos_of(r))
    r=dirs('shared'); rec('ABL shared k=1 BF16',[bf16(W) for W in abl(Ws,r,1.0,1.0)],cos_of(r))
    for fr in [0.75,0.5,0.25]:
        r=dirs('shared'); rec(f'ABL shared k=1 band={fr}',abl(Ws,r,1.0,fr),cos_of(r))
    r=dirs('perlayer'); rec('ABL PER-LAYER kappa=1',abl(Ws,r,1.0,1.0),cos_of(r))
    r=dirs('perlayer'); rec('ABL PER-LAYER kappa=0.7',abl(Ws,r,0.7,1.0),cos_of(r))
    for rho in [0.9,0.8,0.7,0.5]:
        r=dirs('corr',rho); rec(f'ABL corr rho={rho} kappa=0.7',abl(Ws,r,0.7,1.0),cos_of(r))
    for rho in [0.9,0.7]:
        r=dirs('corr',rho); rec(f'ABL corr rho={rho} kappa=1',abl(Ws,r,1.0,1.0),cos_of(r))
    for al in [0.3,1.0,3.0]:
        r=dirs('shared'); rec(f'INJECT shared alpha={al}',inject(Ws,r,al),cos_of(r))
    r=dirs('perlayer'); rec('CTRL rank1 perlayer alpha=1',inject(Ws,r,1.0),cos_of(r))

import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
d, n, L = 256, 1024, 28


def rand_orth(m, k, rg):
    Q, _ = np.linalg.qr(rg.standard_normal((m, k)))
    return Q[:, :k]


def make_W(kind, rg):
    U = rand_orth(d, d, rg)
    V = rand_orth(n, d, rg)
    if kind == 'gauss':
        x = rg.standard_normal((d, n)) / np.sqrt(n)
        s = np.sqrt(np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(x @ x.T))[::-1])
    else:
        s = (np.arange(1, d + 1) ** -0.8)
    return U @ np.diag(s) @ V.T


def bf16(W):
    a = np.ascontiguousarray(W.astype(np.float32)).view(np.uint32)
    a = ((a.astype(np.uint64) + 0x8000) & 0xFFFF0000).astype(np.uint32)
    return a.view(np.float32).astype(np.float64)


def eig(W):
    e, U = np.linalg.eigh(W @ W.T)
    return np.clip(e, 0, None), U


def stats(Ws, k=1, win=8):
    E = [eig(W) for W in Ws]
    Pb = [U[:, :k] @ U[:, :k].T for _, U in E]
    Pt = [U[:, -k:] @ U[:, -k:].T for _, U in E]

    def align(P, w):
        best = 0.0
        for st in range(0, len(P) - w + 1):
            best = max(best, np.linalg.eigvalsh(np.mean(P[st:st + w], axis=0))[-1])
        return best

    botgap = min(np.sqrt(e[0] / e[1]) for e, _ in E)
    G = sum(W @ W.T for W in Ws)
    g = np.linalg.eigvalsh(G)
    Gh = sum(d * (W @ W.T) / np.trace(W @ W.T) for W in Ws) / len(Ws)
    gh = np.linalg.eigvalsh(Gh)
    return dict(G_lmin=g[0] / g.mean(), G_lmax=g[-1] / g.mean(), nG_lmin=gh[0],
                BSA_all=align(Pb, len(Ws)), BSA_w=align(Pb, win),
                TSA_all=align(Pt, len(Ws)), TSA_w=align(Pt, win), botgap=botgap)


def abl(Ws, rl, kappa, frac):
    nl = int(round(frac * len(Ws)))
    return [(np.eye(d) - kappa * np.outer(rl[i], rl[i])) @ W if i < nl else W.copy()
            for i, W in enumerate(Ws)]


def inject(Ws, rl, alpha):
    out = []
    for i, W in enumerate(Ws):
        v = rng.standard_normal(n)
        v /= np.linalg.norm(v)
        out.append(W + alpha * np.sqrt(np.trace(W @ W.T) / d) * np.outer(rl[i], v))
    return out


def dirs(mode, rho=None):
    r0 = rng.standard_normal(d)
    r0 /= np.linalg.norm(r0)
    if mode == 'shared':
        return [r0] * L
    out = []
    for _ in range(L):
        x = rng.standard_normal(d)
        x /= np.linalg.norm(x)
        y = x if mode == 'perlayer' else rho * r0 + np.sqrt(1 - rho ** 2) * x
        out.append(y / np.linalg.norm(y))
    return out


def cos_of(rl):
    M = np.array(rl)
    C = np.abs(M @ M.T)
    iu = np.triu_indices(len(rl), 1)
    return C[iu].mean()


cols = ['G_lmin', 'G_lmax', 'nG_lmin', 'BSA_all', 'BSA_w', 'TSA_w', 'botgap']
for spec in ['gauss', 'heavy']:
    print(f"\n===== honest spectrum = {spec}  (d={d}, fan-in={n}, L={L}, window=8) =====", flush=True)
    Ws = [make_W(spec, rng) for _ in range(L)]
    print(f"{'recipe':<30}{'xlayer_cos':>11}" + "".join(f"{c:>11}" for c in cols), flush=True)

    def rec(name, X, c=None):
        s = stats(X)
        cs = '-' if c is None else f"{c:.3f}"
        print(f"{name:<30}{cs:>11}" + "".join(f"{s[c2]:>11.4g}" for c2 in cols), flush=True)

    rec('HONEST', Ws)
    rec('HONEST bf16', [bf16(W) for W in Ws])
    for kap in [1.0, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3]:
        r = dirs('shared')
        rec(f'ABL shared kappa={kap}', abl(Ws, r, kap, 1.0), cos_of(r))
    r = dirs('shared')
    rec('ABL shared k=1 BF16', [bf16(W) for W in abl(Ws, r, 1.0, 1.0)], cos_of(r))
    for fr in [0.75, 0.5, 0.25]:
        r = dirs('shared')
        rec(f'ABL shared k=1 band={fr}', abl(Ws, r, 1.0, fr), cos_of(r))
    r = dirs('perlayer')
    rec('ABL PER-LAYER kappa=1', abl(Ws, r, 1.0, 1.0), cos_of(r))
    r = dirs('perlayer')
    rec('ABL PER-LAYER kappa=0.7', abl(Ws, r, 0.7, 1.0), cos_of(r))
    for rho in [0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.5]:
        r = dirs('corr', rho)
        rec(f'ABL corr rho={rho} kappa=0.7', abl(Ws, r, 0.7, 1.0), cos_of(r))
    for rho in [0.9, 0.7]:
        r = dirs('corr', rho)
        rec(f'ABL corr rho={rho} kappa=1', abl(Ws, r, 1.0, 1.0), cos_of(r))
    for al in [0.3, 1.0, 3.0]:
        r = dirs('shared')
        rec(f'INJECT shared alpha={al}', inject(Ws, r, al), cos_of(r))
    r = dirs('perlayer')
    rec('CTRL rank1 perlayer alpha=1', inject(Ws, r, 1.0), cos_of(r))
```

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import numpy as np
from analyze import per_layer_svd, botgap_per_layer, subspace_alignment, best_window_alignment, gram_stats, bottom1_vectors, mean_pairwise_abscos

np.random.seed(0)
d = 16
n_layers = 12
# construct a 'planted' common bottom direction across all layers to test BSA
v_common = np.random.randn(d); v_common /= np.linalg.norm(v_common)
mats = {}
for l in range(n_layers):
    A = np.random.randn(d, d) * 1.0
    # project out v_common from column space contributions, then add tiny component along v_common
    U, s, Vt = np.linalg.svd(A)
    s_new = np.sort(np.random.uniform(1, 5, d))[::-1]
    s_new[-1] = 0.001  # force a small singular value
    # force bottom singular vector = v_common
    Uq, _ = np.linalg.qr(np.column_stack([v_common] + [np.random.randn(d) for _ in range(d-1)]))
    Uq[:,0] = v_common
    W = Uq @ np.diag(s_new) @ Vt
    mats[l] = W.astype(np.float32)

svd_dict = per_layer_svd(mats)
gaps = botgap_per_layer(svd_dict)
print('botgap sample:', list(gaps.items())[:3])
bsa1_all = subspace_alignment(svd_dict, 1, 'bottom')
print('BSA1_all (planted common direction, expect near 1.0):', bsa1_all)
bsa1_w8, rng = best_window_alignment(svd_dict, 1, 'bottom', 8)
print('BSA1_w8:', bsa1_w8, rng)
g = gram_stats(mats)
print('gram:', g)
b1 = bottom1_vectors(svd_dict)
cos, mid = mean_pairwise_abscos(b1)
print('mean pairwise abscos (expect ~1.0 since planted common):', cos)

NEW: def load_safetensors_weights(model_dir: Path):
    """Load all self_attn.o_proj.weight and mlp.down_proj.weight tensors as fp32 numpy, grouped by layer idx.
    Uses the torch (CPU-only) framework to safely handle bf16 storage dtype; tensors never touch the GPU
    (torch.cuda is never invoked, .numpy() copies straight from a CPU tensor)."""
    from safetensors import safe_open
    import torch

    st_files = sorted(model_dir.glob("*.safetensors"))
    if not st_files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no safetensors in {model_dir}")

    o_proj = {}
    down_proj = {}
    layer_re = re.compile(r"\.layers\.(\d+)\.")
    for f in st_files:
        with safe_open(str(f), framework="pt", device="cpu") as sf:
            for key in sf.keys():
                if "self_attn.o_proj.weight" in key:
                    m = layer_re.search(key)
                    if m:
                        t = sf.get_tensor(key).to(torch.float32)
                        o_proj[int(m.group(1))] = t.numpy().copy()
                elif "mlp.down_proj.weight" in key:
                    m = layer_re.search(key)
                    if m:
                        t = sf.get_tensor(key).to(torch.float32)
                        down_proj[int(m.group(1))] = t.numpy().copy()
    return o_proj, down_proj
```

# Abliteration recipe census + external benchmark panel reachability

Working dir: `/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_fcYd_7ruOwtm/iter_3/gen_hypo/claude_agent/census/`
Raw data saved alongside this file: `raw_search_results.json` (HF API search dumps), `candidates_all.json`
(418 unique candidate models), `final_ids.json` (50 sampled), `raw_cards.json` (fetched README.md + config.json
text for all 50), `heretic_readme.md`, `heretic_config_default.toml`, `src__heretic__main.py` (heretic's optimizer
source, for the search-space quotes below), `helm_safety_v1.17.0_runs.json`, `helm_airbench_v1.19.0_runs.json`,
`salad_leaderboard.xlsx`.

---

## JOB 1 — Abliteration recipe census

### Sampling
Queried the HF Hub API (`api/models?search=...&full=true`) for `abliterated` (100 hits, capped) and `heretic`
(100 hits, capped), plus `api/models?author=...&full=true` for `huihui-ai` (100, capped), `mlabonne` (100, capped),
`failspy` (33, all), `p-e-w` (26, all). Deduped to 418 unique text-generation, non-private repos. Sized every id by
regex on the repo name (`\d+(\.\d+)?B`), took all 45 that resolved to ≤4B, and added 5 larger reference points
(2×failspy 8B/70B-class, 2×mlabonne 8B, 2×p-e-w gpt-oss-20B) for tool-recipe context → **50 candidates**, then
fetched `https://huggingface.co/<id>/raw/main/README.md` and `.../config.json` for each (all via direct HTTP,
`raw_cards.json`).

**Exclusions after reading the cards** (13 of 50):
- 4 gave HTTP 401 on both README and config (now access-restricted/gated): `huihui-ai/Qwen3-4B-abliterated`,
  `huihui-ai/Qwen3-0.6B-abliterated`, `huihui-ai/Qwen3-1.7B-abliterated`, `huihui-ai/Huihui-MoE-1.3B-A0.6B-abliterated`.
- 3 mlabonne hits (`Gemmalpaca-2B`, `OrcaGemma-2B`, `OrcaGemma-2B-v2`) are plain Alpaca/Orca SFT finetunes with no
  `abliterated` tag — false positives from the author-list query, not abliteration at all.
- 4 huihui-ai `Huihui-MoE-*` hits are expert-merge MoE assemblies ("It has not been fine-tuned…") with no refusal
  removal step — false positives from the author-list query.
- 2 huihui-ai `*-CensorTune` hits are SFT runs that *increase* refusal on 320+ harmful prompts — the opposite
  operation, not abliteration.

**Final census: n = 37 real abliterated/decensored checkpoints**, sizes 0.5B–70B (30 of 37 are ≤4B; median ≈2B).
Every classification below quotes the card text directly; nothing is inferred beyond what's written.

### Recipe groups found (37 cards)

| Group | n | tool (quoted) | direction | strength | layers | healing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Classic FailSpy/mlabonne orthogonalization** | 3 | "Special thanks to @FailSpy for the original code and technique" (huihui-ai/Llama-3.2-3B, mlabonne/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B); failspy's own card: "orthogonalized bfloat16 safetensor weights… based on… 'Refusal in LLMs is mediated by a **single direction**'" | single (explicit) | full/hard projection (orthogonalization removes the direction outright; no scaling term is mentioned) | not explicitly stated as "all layers" in the card text, but the method as described operates uniformly (no layer-subset note, unlike Group C) | none mentioned |
| **B. huihui-ai in-house, no extra note** | 5 | "created with abliteration (see [remove-refusals-with-transformers](https://github.com/Sumandora/remove-refusals-with-transformers)…). This is a crude, proof-of-concept implementation to remove refusals … **without using TransformerLens**. Ablation was performed using a new and faster method…" (verbatim, repeated across cards) | **unstated** | **unstated** | **unstated** | none mentioned |
| **C. huihui-ai in-house, explicit layer-subset note** | 3 | same base template as B | unstated | unstated | **explicit subset, quoted**: `Huihui-MiniCPM5-2B-abliterated`: "Layers 6-37, 40 are being ablated (0-based indexing). This is just a new ablation method of ours, aimed at probing which layers have a greater impact"; `Huihui-NeoHorse-1-4B-abliterated` (+ its GGUF repost): "Layers 5-17 are being ablated (0-based indexing)." | none mentioned |
| **D. heretic, full parameter table published** | 10 | `[Heretic](https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic) v1.0.0`–`v1.4.0` | **8/10 numeric `direction_index`** (a float layer position, e.g. 30.93, 16.83, 20.01, 18.58 — global/interpolated, i.e. effectively single-direction); **2/10 explicit `per layer`** (`Abiray/MiniCPM5-2B-heretic-abliterated-GGUF`, `p-e-w/gpt-oss-20b-heretic-v3`) | **0/10 at flat weight=1.0.** Every `attn.o_proj.max_weight` sampled is >1.0 (range 1.05–1.50 across the 9 I could parse numerically), and `min_weight` is a *different* number from `max_weight` in every case (a decaying kernel, not a constant) | not "all layers" as a uniform choice — heretic always fits a **position-dependent weight kernel** (`max_weight_position`, `min_weight_distance`) per component, so weight is layer-varying by construction even when direction is global | none mentioned |
| **E. heretic named, no parameter table in this card** | 4 | explicit "Heretic vX.Y.Z" (`DavidAU/gemma-3-1b-it-heretic…`, `DreamFast/qwen3-4b-heretic` — also states "Trials: 200, Trial Selected: Trial 96", confirming the default `n_trials=200`, `saidutta69/lfm2.5-2.6b…heretic`, `sillykiwi/…heretic…GGUF` which quantizes a heretic-tagged base) | unstated in-card (parameters live only in the underlying repo, not this card) | unstated | unstated | none |
| **F. huihui-ai post-abliteration SFT healing** | 4 | base recipe unstated (inherits from a parent huihui-ai abliterated repo); healing step: "Finetuned from model: huihui-ai/Qwen2.5-{0.5B,3B}-Instruct-abliterated… Dataset used to train: huihui-ai/Guilherme34_uncensor… SFT with Unsloth" | unstated | unstated | unstated | **explicit SFT**, quoted above |
| **G. mlabonne DPO healing** | 1 | `NeuralDaredevil-8B-abliterated`: "This is a DPO fine-tune of mlabonne/Daredevil-8-abliterated… **The DPO fine-tuning successfully recovers the performance loss due to the abliteration process**" | unstated (inherited) | unstated | unstated | **explicit DPO**, quoted above |
| **H. fully unstated (third-party requant/rehost)** | 7 | e.g. `mondk`/`0xSojalSec` stub cards: *"This is an uncensored version of openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B created with abliteration."* — full stop, no tool/direction/strength/layer/healing info at all; `bartowski`, `xunlinkx`, `nqd145`, `SC117` are GGUF/MLX/LiteRT requantizations that only cite a parent repo; `Andycurrent` names "Heretic" in the title but the body gives no verifiable methodology detail | unstated | unstated | unstated | unstated |

*(3+5+3+10+4+4+1+7 = 37)*

### The three requested fractions (of n = 37)

- **Full-strength + single-direction + all-layer + no-healing (as literally, jointly stated in the card)**:
  **3/37 = 8.1%** (Group A). Caveat for honesty: even these 3 cards don't literally write the words "all layers" —
  they just don't mention any layer restriction, unlike Group C. If you require the *positive* statement "applied
  to every layer," the true count is **0/37** — no card in the sample explicitly claims uniform full-strength
  application across all layers; the closest evidence is Group A's silence on any subset.
- **Explicitly say per-layer**: **2/37 = 5.4%** for per-layer *direction* (`direction_index = per layer`, Group D).
  Separately, **3/37 = 8.1%** explicitly name a *layer subset/band* being ablated (Group C: "Layers 6-37,40" /
  "Layers 5-17" — a different, huihui-specific, form of layer-non-uniformity, layer selection rather than
  per-layer direction). Combined, **5/37 = 13.5%** state some form of explicit layer-non-uniformity. On top of
  that, **10/37 = 27%** (Group D) come from a tool (heretic) whose ablation-strength kernel is *always*
  layer-varying by construction, whether or not the direction itself is per-layer — so if "per-layer" is read as
  "strength varies by layer" rather than "direction varies by layer," the true floor is closer to **13/37 = 35%**
  (Groups C+D).
- **Unstated** (direction AND strength AND layer-scope all unspecified in the card): **Groups B+E+F+G+H = 5+4+4+1+7
  = 21/37 = 56.8%**. If "unstated" is scoped narrowly to *only* cards with literally zero recipe detail beyond the
  word "abliteration" (Groups B+H): **12/37 = 32.4%**.

**Honest summary**: the "unstated" bucket is the biggest single bucket by a wide margin under any reasonable
reading (33–57% depending on strictness), confirming the card text is a poor and inconsistent source for recipe
parameters for roughly a third to a majority of real Hub checkpoints. What *could* recover this instead of the
card: (1) for `heretic`-made models, the exact per-model optimized parameters are deterministically re-derivable
by loading the model and finding the orthogonalized subspace / weight-scaling per layer directly from the
safetensors weights (rank-1 structure of the edit + the kernel shape), since heretic bakes them into the weights,
not just the card — cross-checked in our prior Gram-scar work (`project_qwen3_safety_genhypo_iter2_run_fcYd_7ruOwtm.md`);
(2) for huihui-ai's "new and faster method" (Groups B/C), the ablated layer range is directly recoverable by
diffing per-layer weight norms/ranks against the unablated parent checkpoint (Group C shows this is *sometimes*
a proper subset, so the diff is not guaranteed to be "all layers" and must be checked per-model); (3) `torch_dtype`
is always readable from `config.json` regardless of what the card says (see below).

### dtype (from `config.json`, n = 37)
- **bfloat16: 12**, **float16: 1**, **no config.json / not determinable from the card's repo (GGUF/MLX/LiteRT-only
  repos, or config fetch failed): 24**. Of the 13 with a resolvable dtype, 12/13 = 92% are bfloat16 — consistent
  with heretic's default dtype list `["auto" (≈bfloat16), "float16", "bfloat16", "float32"]` and huihui-ai's own
  loading scripts, which default to `torch.bfloat16`.

---

### heretic (p-e-w/heretic) verbatim defaults — GitHub README + `config.default.toml` + `src/heretic/main.py`

Fetched `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/p-e-w/heretic/master/README.md`,
`.../config.default.toml`, and `.../src/heretic/main.py` (the actual Optuna objective — the numeric bounds are
**not** exposed as a single static "default" in the config file; they are the search space the optimizer explores
every run).

**What it optimizes** (README, verbatim):
> "Heretic is a tool that removes censorship (aka "safety alignment") from transformer-based language models
> without expensive post-training. It combines an advanced implementation of directional ablation, also known as
> "abliteration" (Arditi et al. 2024)... with a **TPE-based parameter optimizer powered by Optuna**... Heretic
> finds high-quality abliteration parameters by **co-minimizing the number of refusals and the KL divergence**
> from the original model."
> "The process is fully automatic and does not require configuration."

`config.default.toml` (verbatim, the actual run defaults):
```
n_trials = 200
n_startup_trials = 60
scorers = [
    { plugin = "heretic.scorers.keyword_rate.KeywordRate", optimization = "minimize"},
    { plugin = "heretic.scorers.kl_divergence.KLDivergence", optimization = "minimize"},
]
orthogonalize_direction = true
row_normalization = "full"
```
So by default: **200 trials, 60 random-startup trials, two co-minimized objectives (refusal-keyword rate and KL
divergence)** — a genuine multi-objective Bayesian/TPE search, not a fixed recipe.

**Is `per layer` direction the default, or an option?** From `src/heretic/main.py` (verbatim):
```python
direction_scope = trial.suggest_categorical(
    "direction_scope",
    [
        "global",
        "per layer",
    ],
)
...
direction_index = trial.suggest_float(
    "direction_index",
    0.4 * last_layer_index,
    0.9 * last_layer_index,
)
if direction_scope == "per layer":
    direction_index = None
```
So **`direction_scope` is itself a searched hyperparameter, not a fixed default** — Optuna picks "global" vs
"per layer" per trial (across 200 trials, 60 of them uniform-random exploration) and keeps whichever wins the
co-minimization. "global" direction_index, when chosen, is a **continuous float** sampled uniformly in
`[0.4×last_layer, 0.9×last_layer]`, and non-integer values are linearly interpolated between the two nearest
layers' directions (README: "The residual direction index is a float rather than an integer... This unlocks a
vast space of additional directions beyond the ones identified by the difference-of-means computation"). In our
37-card sample of shipped heretic models, this resolved to **global 8/10 times, per-layer 2/10 times** — so
per-layer is a real, reachable, non-default-but-not-rare outcome of the search, not a fixed option a user toggles.

**Weight-kernel parameters — are `max_weight`/`min_weight` etc. fixed defaults, or searched?** Verbatim (also
searched per trial, per component `attn.o_proj` and `mlp.down_proj` separately):
```python
max_weight_lower_bound = -0.25 if component == "mlp.down_proj" else 0.8
max_weight = max(0.0, trial.suggest_float(f"{component}.max_weight", max_weight_lower_bound, 1.5))
max_weight_position = trial.suggest_float(f"{component}.max_weight_position", 0.6*last_layer_index, 1.0*last_layer_index)
min_weight = trial.suggest_float(f"{component}.min_weight", 0.0, 1.0)   # sampled as a FRACTION of max_weight
min_weight_distance = trial.suggest_float(f"{component}.min_weight_distance", 1.0, max(0.6*last_layer_index, 1.0))
parameters[component] = AbliterationParameters(
    max_weight=max_weight,
    max_weight_position=max_weight_position,
    min_weight=(min_weight * max_weight),
    min_weight_distance=min_weight_distance,
)
```
So **there is no single fixed `max_weight=1.0` default** — the search space for attention's `max_weight` is
`[0.8, 1.5]` and for MLP's is `[max(0, -0.25), 1.5]` (i.e. MLP can be driven to exactly 0 = untouched, with
"positive probability mass on exactly 0" per an in-code comment referencing issue #202: "Ablating the MLP is
often unnecessary for removing refusals and tends to damage model intelligence more... so on many models the
optimum is to leave it (mostly) untouched"). The kernel is **always layer-position-dependent** by construction
(a peak at `max_weight_position` decaying to `min_weight` over `min_weight_distance` layers) — this is not an
optional feature, it's the only mode heretic has; there is no "constant weight across all layers" mode at all.
Empirically in our 9 numerically-parsed shipped models, attn `max_weight` ranged **1.05–1.50** (never exactly
1.0, never below 1.0) and `min_weight` differed from `max_weight` in every case (range 0.65–1.50), confirming
the kernel is never flat in practice either.

**Bottom line for the hypothesis under test**: per-layer direction and non-unit/layer-varying weight are **not**
rare deviations from a heretic "default" — non-unit, layer-position-varying weight is the *only* mode heretic has
(there is no flat-weight-1.0-all-layers option in the tool at all), and per-layer *direction* specifically is
chosen by the optimizer in a genuine (not rigged) 2-of-10 rate in our sample, exactly matching its being one of
two co-equal categorical options in the search space.

**Net for Job 2**: (a) SALAD-Bench and (b)/(c) HELM releases are real, live, immediately downloadable panels but
each contributes only **1–3 sub-4B open-weight checkpoints** — far too thin on their own to ground-truth a
sub-4B-focused study; (d) SORRY-Bench is reachable for prompts only, not a usable numeric panel without re-running

### JOB 1 — Abliteration recipe census (n=37 real checkpoints, after excluding 13 false positives/401s from an initial 50)

Sampled via HF API (`abliterated`, `heretic` searches + huihui-ai/mlabonne/failspy/p-e-w author listings), fetched every README.md + config.json directly.

**Three requested fractions:**
- **Full-strength + single-direction + all-layer + no-healing (jointly stated)**: 3/37 = 8.1% (classic FailSpy/mlabonne orthogonalization lineage) — and even these never literally write "all layers," they just don't mention a subset.
- **Explicitly per-layer**: 2/37 = 5.4% for per-layer *direction* (heretic's `direction_index = per layer`); separately 3/37 = 8.1% name an explicit layer *subset* (huihui-ai: "Layers 6-37,40" / "Layers 5-17"). Combined explicit layer-non-uniformity: 5/37 = 13.5%.
- **Unstated**: 21/37 = 56.8% broadly (any of direction/strength/layer-scope unspecified); 12/37 = 32.4% narrowly (zero recipe detail beyond the word "abliteration," e.g. identical stub cards: *"This is an uncensored version of openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B created with abliteration."*).

**Heretic verbatim defaults** (from GitHub `README.md` + `config.default.toml` + `src/heretic/main.py`): 200 trials, 60 random-startup, TPE/Optuna co-minimizing refusal-keyword-rate and KL-divergence. Critically, `direction_scope` (`"global"` vs `"per layer"`) is itself `trial.suggest_categorical(...)` — a searched hyperparameter, not a fixed default — and the weight kernel (`max_weight` ∈ [0.8,1.5] for attention, ∈[-0.25,1.5] for MLP; `min_weight`, `max_weight_position`, `min_weight_distance`) is **always** layer-position-varying by construction; there is no flat-weight-1.0-all-layers mode in the tool at all. Empirically in shipped models, attn `max_weight` was never exactly 1.0 (range 1.05–1.50).

However, LoRA adapters are shared through open repositories like Hugging Face Hub \\citep{huggingface_hub_docs}, making them vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Current detection methods require running the model with test input data -- making them impractical for screening thousands of adapters where the trigger for backdoor behavior is unknown. We detect poisoned adapters by analyzing their weight matrices directly, without running the model -- making our method trigger-agnostic. For each attention projection (Q, K, V, O), our method extracts five spectral statistics from the low-rank update $\\Delta W$, yielding a 20-dimensional signature for each adapter. A logistic regression detector trained on this representation separates benign and poisoned adapters across three model families -- Llama-3.2-3B~\\citep{llama3}, Qwen2.5-3B~\\citep{qwen25}, and Gemma-2-2B~\\citep{gemma2} -- on unseen test adapters drawn from instruction-following, reasoning, question-answering, code, and classification tasks. Across all three architectures, the detector achieves 100\\% accuracy. \n\nSubjects: |  Cryptography and Security (cs.CR); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL); Machine Existing moderation relies on metadata or generated outputs, but metadata can be deceptive and generating outputs may itself be unacceptable or illegal. We show that a safer signal lives in the weights. The top-left singular vectors of a LoRA's updates form a compact, inference-free fingerprint ($u_1$) of its strongest learned change. Using human-subject age as a benign proxy for CSAM, we find that $u_1$ identifies what a LoRA was trained on, generalizes across base models, and abstains on unrelated benign content. The signal is robust to additive weight noise, rescaling, and precision reduction. These results indicate that harmful LoRAs could be screened directly from their weights without relying on metadata or generating harmful outputs. \n\nSubjects: |  Machine Learning (cs.LG); Computers For each residual-write matrix take the projector onto its bottom-k (or top-k) LEFT\n  singular subspace, average those projectors over a contiguous band of layers, and take the largest\n  eigenvalue: BOTTOM- and TOP-SUBSPACE ALIGNMENT. A projector discards singular values entirely, so the\n  statistic is invariant to each layer's spectrum; it is windowed, so an edit confined to part of the\n  stack is found rather than diluted; and it is a continuous overlap, so it degrades gracefully.   healing stage followed. Then, from the WEIGHTS alone, recover each layer's suppressed direction as its
  bottom left singular vector and measure (1) the realised ablation strength, (2) which layers were
  touched, and (3) the mean pairwise cosine between those directions across layers. Report the FRACTION
  that are full-strength single-direction all-layer. If that fraction is small, the scar as originally
  specified detects one recipe, and that is stated BEFORE the ladder is graded rather than discovered
  after. The cross-layer cosine is the number that decides whether the graded subspace statistic
  survives, and it is measured, not assumed.
  (ii) THE INSTRUMENT. Compute bottom- and top-subspace alignment, and the local rank-deficiency ratio,
  on every census checkpoint and on a first slice of the honest panel, plus on two edits we construct
  ourselves - one rank-one injection at the published method's own alpha, one abliteration - on a
  checkpoint we control. Validate the honest baseline on real weights, not on Gaussian simulation. The
  pre-registered withdrawal path is unchanged and now finer-grained: if the sharing statistic fails, it
  is withdrawn for that rung and plain forgery cost is reported there; if the local statistic also
  fails on real full-strength abliterations, the whole detection axis is withdrawn and the study reverts
  to the plain cost ladder plus R1, which remains a complete deliverable.
NEW:   (i) THE RECIPE CENSUS. The card half of this is ALREADY DONE and its numbers are in H3 claim 3c: 37
  real abliterated Hub checkpoints read, 8.1 percent matching the recipe the previous statistic required,
  5.4 percent stating a per-layer direction, 56.8 percent stating no recipe at all. Stage 0 completes it
  from the WEIGHTS, which is where the 56.8 percent has to be resolved: for each census checkpoint recover
  every layer's suppressed direction as its bottom left singular vector, then measure the realised
  ablation strength, which layers were touched, and the mean pairwise cosine across layers. That cosine is
  the axis H3 grades the instrument on, so it is measured on real artifacts before anything is built on it.
  One census by-product is kept as a free positive control: the same author ships checkpoints fine-tuned to
  INCREASE refusal, which are a ready-made real-world blanket-refuser anchor for H5's poles.
  (ii) THE INSTRUMENT ON REAL WEIGHTS. Compute bottom- and top-subspace alignment and the local
  rank-deficiency ratio on every census checkpoint and on a first slice of the honest panel, plus on two
  edits we construct ourselves on a checkpoint we control - one rank-one injection at the published
  method's own alpha, one abliteration. The honest baseline is validated on real weights, not on
  simulation. The withdrawal path is finer-grained than before: if the sharing statistic fails, it is
  withdrawn for that rung and plain forgery cost is reported there; if the local statistic also fails on
  real full-strength abliterations, the whole detection axis is withdrawn and the study reverts to the
  plain cost ladder plus R1, which remains a complete deliverable.
  NOTE ON THE ANCHOR, found in the census and worth stating because it changes Stage 1's model list: the
  best-known abliterated Qwen3 checkpoints from one publisher now return 401 and are no longer openly
  downloadable, so the anchor lineage's abliterated member is taken from a still-open alternative produced
  by the automated tool, with the gated ones used only if access is granted.

NEW: H3, THE EDIT-RANK LAW. (a) Exact invariance holds for linear reads at the injection layer, to numerical
precision, in fp32 before any behavioural work. (b) Metrics read downstream of a normalisation move by less
than 0.05 correlation units under the constant rung, with the measured deviation reported. (c) The rank-one
rung moves across-item coupling where the constant rung does not, and abliteration, being item-dependent,
moves levels and LOWERS coupling - filed in advance and scored for free against real abliterated
checkpoints. (d) THE INSTRUMENT, with thresholds pre-registered from the simulation already run rather
than from a hope. On real checkpoints, windowed bottom-subspace alignment must separate edited from honest
with held-out-family AUROC of at least 0.9 at zero prompts and no parent, using a threshold fixed in
advance at 0.35 - roughly twice the simulated honest value of 0.177, and below the 0.358 the statistic
reaches at the weakest correlated recipe simulated. It must still separate at an ablation weight of 0.7
and on a half-stack band, which is precisely where the old raw-Gram statistic sat inside honest range. Its
behaviour is reported as a CURVE in the measured cross-layer cosine, with the census locating real
checkpoints on that curve. The local rank-deficiency ratio must separate full-strength projections
regardless of sharing, against a bf16-realistic separator of 0.1 rather than an exact algebraic zero,
since bf16 rounding lifts a projected matrix's ratio to about 0.010 against an honest 0.997. The
per-layer-random arm stays as the negative control and is EXPECTED to be at chance for the sharing
statistic; that is the definitional boundary and is reported as such, not as a failure. The injection half
is pre-registered as the weaker one on measured grounds: fixed top-1 alignment detects a shared injection
on a Gaussian stack but not on a heavy-tailed one at the same magnitude, so the statistic is swept over
spectral rank bands and graded at the published method's own alpha, and if it fails there the detection
axis is withdrawn for that rung.
If the sharing half fails on real checkpoints, the detection axis is withdrawn for that rung and plain
forgery cost is reported there. If the local half also fails, THE WHOLE DETECTION AXIS IS WITHDRAWN, the
headline quantity reverts to plain forgery cost, and the paper's claim becomes R1 plus the plain ladder
plus a reportable negative about parent-free weight auditing - which, given a published per-layer
parent-free attempt already reported inconsistent success, is a finding rather than a hole. A third
outcome is live and would be the most useful of all: that the recovered RECIPE - direction sharing,
realised strength, layer band - predicts measured harmful compliance, which would make the detection
column a graded safety read rather than a binary tamper flag.

## THE CENTRAL REPAIR — SUBSPACE ALIGNMENT REPLACES THE RAW GRAM SCAR

The reviewer killed the iter-2 statistic (`lambda_min/mean` of `G = sum_l W_l W_l^T`): it reads
MAGNITUDE, so the honest baseline swings with the spectrum, and it fires for only one recipe.
**New statistic (MEASURED, not asserted — `sim/bsa2.py`, d=256, fan-in=1024, L=28, window=8):**
BSA = largest eigenvalue of the mean over a contiguous layer window of `P_l`, the projector onto
layer l's **bottom-k LEFT singular subspace**. TSA = same on the top-k. BOTGAP = per-layer
`s_min/s_2ndmin`. A projector discards singular values ⇒ spectrum-invariant BY CONSTRUCTION.

| recipe | old G_lmin (gauss / heavy) | **BSA_w8 (gauss / heavy)** | botgap (heavy) |
|---|---|---|---|
| HONEST | **0.821 / 0.119** (7x swing!) | **0.168 / 0.177** (invariant) | 0.997 |
| ABL shared kappa=1 | 1e-16 | 1.000 | 0.000 |
| ABL shared **kappa=0.7** | 0.089 / 0.027 | **0.969 / 0.953** | 0.446 |
| ABL shared kappa=0.5 | 0.248 / 0.073 | 0.866 / 0.845 | 0.713 |
| ABL shared kappa=0.3 | 0.486 / 0.116 | 0.268 / **0.617** | 0.905 |
| ABL **band=75%** | 0.252 / 0.078 | **1.000** | 0.000 |
| ABL **band=50%** | 0.489 / 0.105 | **1.000** | 0.000 |
| ABL band=25% | 0.722 / 0.119 | 0.876 | 0.000 |
| ABL **PER-LAYER kappa=1** | 0.819 / 0.120 (=honest) | 0.183 / 0.173 (**BLIND**) | **0.000** |
| ABL PER-LAYER kappa=0.7 | =honest | 0.169 (BLIND) | **0.435** |
| ABL corr cos=.81 kappa=.7 | 0.249 | **0.820 / 0.805** | 0.42 |
| ABL corr cos=.65 | 0.394 | 0.678 / 0.673 | 0.44 |
| ABL corr cos=.48 | 0.524 | 0.562 / 0.533 | 0.43 |
| ABL corr cos=.25 | 0.720 | 0.362 / 0.358 | 0.45 |
| **bf16 shared kappa=1** | 2.74e-6 | 1.000 | **0.0103** (NOT 0) |
| INJECT shared a=1 | TSA 0.664 (gauss) | | |
| INJECT shared a=1 **heavy** | **TSA 0.167 = honest — INVISIBLE** | | |
| INJECT shared a=3 heavy | TSA 0.167 — still invisible | | |
| CTRL rank1 per-layer rand | TSA 0.177 = honest | | |

**KEY WINS:** (1) spectrum invariance is real; (2) **WINDOWING completely solves layer bands**
(1.000 at 50%) — consistent with [[project-steering-windowed-w05w-iter5-exec]]; (3) BSA is
**monotone in the cross-layer cosine**, so "per-layer" is a graded axis, not a cliff; (4) BOTGAP
catches per-layer abliteration that BSA is blind to, even at kappa=0.7.
**HONEST REMAINDER:** the blind corner is per-layer direction AND kappa<1 together. And the
**INJECTION half fails under heavy tails** at top-1 (the injected dir never reaches the top of a
heavy-tailed spectrum) ⇒ must sweep spectral RANK BANDS; pre-register ROSI's own alpha.

## ABLITERATION RECIPE CENSUS (n=37 real Hub ckpts, cards+configs fetched)
- **only 3/37 = 8.1%** jointly state full-strength + single-direction + all-layer + no healing
  (0/37 if a positive "all layers" statement is required) ⇒ **the iter-2 statistic covered <1/10**
- **2/37 = 5.4%** explicitly per-layer DIRECTION; **3/37 = 8.1%** explicit layer BAND
  (huihui: "Layers 6-37,40", "Layers 5-17"); **21/37 = 56.8% unstated**, 12/37 zero detail
- **heretic**: `direction_scope` global-vs-per-layer is a **`trial.suggest_categorical` SEARCHED
  hyperparameter**, not a default; 200 Optuna/TPE trials co-minimizing refusal-keyword rate + KL;
  the weight kernel is **ALWAYS layer-position-varying — there is NO flat-weight-1.0 mode**;
  shipped attn `max_weight` 1.05–1.50, **never exactly 1.0** (i.e. OVER-ablation kappa>1 is common).
  **8/10** heretic cards with parameter tables used a **numeric (global) `direction_index`.**
- **huihui-ai/Qwen3-{4B,1.7B,0.6B}-abliterated are now GATED (401)** ⇒ anchor lineage needs another
  abliterated Qwen3-4B (e.g. `DreamFast/qwen3-4b-heretic`, which exists and states Trials:200).
- FREE POSITIVE CONTROL FOUND: huihui `*-CensorTune` models are SFT'd to **INCREASE** refusal
  ⇒ a real-world blanket-refuser anchor for the "must lose" pole.

## EXTERNAL SAFETY NUMBERS — THE REVIEWER'S FIX ONLY PARTLY WORKS
| source | status | n models | **sub-4B** | over-refusal col |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SALAD-Bench xlsx | 200 OK | 34 | **3** | NO |
| HELM Safety v1.17.0 (435 runs) | 200 OK | 87 | **1** (ibm/granite-4.0-micro 3.40B) | **YES, `xstest`** |

| SORRY-Bench | prompts only | — | 0 | — |

⇒ sub-4B safety numbers really are **~6-8 total** (iter-2's pessimism was closer to right than the
reviewer's "6-8 then 30-50"). **The correlation must come from the 7-8B+ HELM stratum run
WEIGHT-ONLY + CPU-PREFILL (~25-40 open-weight after removing API-only).** Capability is abundant.
HELM's `xstest` scenario = a PUBLISHED two-sided ground truth ⇒ kills "the two-sided target is our invention".

## OTHER ITER-3 FIXES SHIPPED
- **Two access tiers** for detection: Tier A reference-free (template content, generation_config
  content, **state-dict key/shape vs the architecture in config.json**, weight statistic) = HEADLINE;
  Tier B = family diff. The tier GAP is its own result.
- **F2a built WITHOUT a new tensor** (Qwen3 has no o_proj/down_proj bias) — carried on a
  massive-activation/attention-sink coordinate; else reported as hygiene like F0.
- **H2 = mixed model** w/ class random effect (within + between components), min class size 10,
  battery designed with >=15 distinct across-item forms. (Within-Spearman needs |rho|>=.73 at n=8.)
- **Exchange rate defined for TEXT rungs too** (graded preamble token ladder) ⇒ no selection on the IV.
- Honest panel: **N>=120 floor**, ~2-4 min/ckpt, ABOVE the training rungs in the shrink order.
- **R1 promoted to co-headline**: the request's step-3 held-out 3-way table, with the
  LEVEL-vs-ACROSS-ITEM split as the pre-registered mechanism.
- New cites: **2508.00161 Remark 3.2** (published parent-free per-layer negative — position BSA as the
  CROSS-layer fix), 2607.01854 (same matrices, per-layer, on Delta W = parent-dependent),
  2608.07786 + 2511.06390 (parent-free spectral but LINEAGE task), **2602.02132** (over-refusal under
  refusal-direction steering ⇒ H6(a) re-aimed to the quantitative REVERSAL at ROSI's own alpha).

**GOTCHA THAT COST 15 MIN:** `np.linalg.svd(256x1024, full_matrices=False)` took **1.09 s** under BLAS
contention. Use `eigh(W @ W.T)` (d x d) for LEFT singular subspaces — ~50x faster.
**ALSO:** `for p in $(pgrep -f "sim/bsa"); do kill $p; done` **killed my own shell** (its command line

{"stdout": "warning: The `fitz` API is deprecated and will be removed in future. Use `import pymupdf` instead.\nURL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JolanMc/Jorak/main/README.md\nType: HTML\nLength: 16940 chars (truncated)\n\n--- Content ---\n\n# Model Scanner\n\n[](LICENSE) [](https://github.com/JolanMc/Jorak/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n\n> 🇫🇷 Version française : **[README_FR.md](README_FR.md)** **Reference-free** detection of **abliteration** in open-source LLMs — determining whether a model has been \"uncensored\" through directional ablation (Arditi et al. 2024 ; Heretic / Reaper / mlabonne) **without access to the original model**. **Principle.** Abliteration orthogonalizes the refusal direction `r̂` out of the weights that write into the residual stream (`o_proj`, `down_proj`): `W' = (I − r̂r̂ᵀ)W`, so `r̂ᵀW' = 0`. The detectable signature = a **live refusal axis that is disconnected from the weights**, a combination that no fine-tuning reproduces. **Output.** A provenance label — `censored` / `ablated` / `finetuned_decensored` / `ambiguous` — plus a confidence score and the affected layers. ## The signature at a glance  |   \n---|---  \n> **The smoking gun** is the bottom row — per-layer weight alignment to the refusal > direction. It stays **near-zero for a censored** model (left, `conf 0.75`) but is > **lit up across layers for an abliterated** one (right, `conf 0.81`) — a signature > ordinary fine-tuning does not leave. Same base model, opposite verdict. ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. Install (see Installation for the conda details) conda env create -f environment.yml && conda activate modelscanner pip install -e \".[dev]\" # 2. Scan a model → verdict printed in the terminal modelscanner scan Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --behavioral # 3. Full branded report (EN+FR HTML + CSVs) under ./_jorak_/ modelscanner scan Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --report ``` Prefer menus over flags? Run **`modelscanner tui`** (full-screen wizard). The rest of this README is reference — start above, dig in below. ## Jorak — three detection techniques **Jorak** is the project (this scanner and the report it produces). It is not a single metric but a bundle of **three complementary detection techniques**, one per angle of attack: \\- **Weights — spectral signature (SVD)** (the *smoking-gun*, CPU, no inference). Three signals: **global** alignment `A` (full ablation), **band** alignment `B` (localized/stealthy ablation, Heretic-style), and **subspace** alignment `S` (bottom-`k` shared subspace — catches **multi-direction** ablation, e.g. OBLITERATUS `n_directions > 1`, which a single `u_min` dilutes). \\- **Activations — axis health (Cohen's d)**: \"is the refusal axis live?\". \\- **Behavioral — refusal rate** (and harmless over-refusal): separates censored from fine-tuned, and flags **evasive ablation** — norm-preserving multi-direction that leaves the weights looking intact to the SVD signature but the behavior damaged (strong live axis + complies on harmful + incoherent over-refusal / uneven multilingual refusal). > **Naming.** `svd_alignment` (signal `A`) is just **one signal of the weights technique** — > not to be confused with **Jorak**, which names the whole project (all three techniques and > the report bundle it emits). ## Pipeline ![Model Scanner pipeline](docs/pipeline.png) End-to-end flow, from a model to a `ScanResult`: the airtight `loaders/` + `probes/`, the three techniques (**weights/SVD** always on, **activations** and **behavioral** optional), `classify()` into 4 buckets, then the views (report, profile, CLI, viz) and the `experiments/` orchestration. Annotated walkthrough: [`docs/PIPELINE.md`](docs/PIPELINE.md). ## Architecture ``` modelscanner/ ├── core/types.py # ScanResult, ModelHandle, enums (airtight boundary) ├── loaders/ # safetensors -> ModelHandle ; arch_adapter ; oracle (dev) ├── probes/ # harmful/harmless probes (6 languages) + per-family templates ├── activations/ # scan-once: hidden states at the last token ├── directions/ # per-layer r̂ (mean-diff) ├── metrics/ # axis_health · jorak (A + band + subspace) · behavioral ├── classifier/ # scan() · classify() · Thresholds -> 4 buckets ├── viz/ # per-layer heatmaps · provenance scatter ├── profile.py # model profile (behavior, quality, hallucination, metadata) ├── report.py # JSON logger (flags + stats + Q/A) └── cli.py # `modelscanner scan` experiments/ # run_scan.py (YAML runner) · run_campaign.sh (one-command launcher) · aggregate.py · campaign_report.py · figures docs/ # HOW_TO_USE · PROTOCOLE_TEST · AWS_RUNBOOK · rapport.tex · presentation tests/ # 125 offline tests + real e2e (gated MS_E2E=1) ``` Two invariants: an **airtight boundary** (`metrics/` never knows where the model comes from) and **scan-once** (a single forward pass → a rich `ScanResult` → views, no recomputation). ## Supported & unsupported model types The scanner loads **safetensors / `.bin` weights** via `transformers` and reads the text decoder (`o_proj` / `down_proj` per layer). What works, and what to do otherwise: | Case | Status | What to do | |---|---|---| | Llama / **Mistral · Ministral** (`mistral`, `ministral`) / **Qwen2 · Qwen3** / Gemma 2·3 (text) | ✅ supported | `modelscanner scan ` | | `config.json` **without `model_type`** (e.g. many `huihui-ai` repos) | ✅ auto-handled | `model_type` is inferred from `architectures` (`[\"Qwen3ForCausalLM\"]` → `qwen3`) | | Unknown family but standard `*.self_attn.o_proj` naming | ✅ auto-detected | weight paths are auto-detected on the loaded model | | **`mistral3`** multimodal (e.g. Ministral-3-8B-2512) | ⚠️ needs transformers upgrade | `pip install -U \"transformers>=5.2.0\"` on the box — then it loads: the registry knows `mistral3` and the loader falls back to `AutoModelForImageTextToText` to reach the nested text decoder. | | `model_type` **too new** for the installed `transformers` | ⚠️ upgrade | `pip install -U transformers` → error `transformers_outdated` | | **GGUF** (`*.gguf`, gguf-only repos) | ⛔ not supported | choose a safetensors variant — GGUF has no dequantizable tensors for Jorak | | bnb 4/8-bit, AWQ, MLX, FP8 quantized | ⛔ not supported (J1) | load a full-precision (fp16/bf16/fp32) checkpoint | Failures are reported with a precise `error_kind` (`gguf_only`, `", "stderr": "", "interrupted": false, "isImage": false, "noOutputExpected": false}
````

OLD: def load_safetensors_weights(model_dir: Path):
    """Load all self_attn.o_proj.weight and mlp.down_proj.weight tensors as fp32 numpy, grouped by layer idx.

    import torch

    st_files = sorted(model_dir.glob("*.safetensors"))

                    if m:

                        down_proj[int(m.group(1))] = t.numpy().copy()
    return o_proj, down_proj
NEW: _ST_DTYPE_ITEMSIZE = {
    "F64": (np.float64, 8),
    "F32": (np.float32, 4),
    "F16": (np.float16, 2),
    "BF16": (np.uint16, 2),  # special-cased below (manual bit conversion, no torch/ml_dtypes needed)
    "I64": (np.int64, 8),
    "I32": (np.int32, 4),
    "I16": (np.int16, 2),
    "I8": (np.int8, 1),
    "U8": (np.uint8, 1),
    "BOOL": (np.bool_, 1),
}


def _bf16_bytes_to_fp32(raw: bytes, n_elements: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """bfloat16 is exactly the top 16 bits of an IEEE-754 float32 (truncated, no exponent bias
    change), so converting is a pure bit-shift: zero-extend each uint16 into the high half of a
    uint32 and reinterpret as float32. No torch / ml_dtypes needed."""
    u16 = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype="<u2", count=n_elements)
    u32 = u16.astype(np.uint32) << 16
    return u32.view(np.float32)


def _read_safetensors_file(path: Path):
    """Manually parse the safetensors container: 8-byte LE header-length, then a JSON header
    {tensor_name: {dtype, shape, data_offsets:[start,end]}}, then a flat data blob.
    Pure Python/numpy, CPU only, never touches the GPU, and needs no torch dependency."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        header_len = int(np.frombuffer(f.read(8), dtype="<u8")[0])
        header_json = f.read(header_len)
        header = json.loads(header_json)
        data_start = 8 + header_len
        tensors = {}
        for name, meta in header.items():
            if name == "__metadata__":
                continue
            dtype_str = meta["dtype"]
            shape = meta["shape"]
            start, end = meta["data_offsets"]
            f.seek(data_start + start)
            raw = f.read(end - start)
            n_elements = int(np.prod(shape)) if shape else 1
            if dtype_str == "BF16":
                arr = _bf16_bytes_to_fp32(raw, n_elements)
            else:
                np_dtype, itemsize = _ST_DTYPE_ITEMSIZE[dtype_str]
                arr = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype=np_dtype, count=n_elements).astype(np.float32)
            tensors[name] = arr.reshape(shape) if shape else arr
        return tensors


def load_safetensors_weights(model_dir: Path):
    """Load all self_attn.o_proj.weight and mlp.down_proj.weight tensors as fp32 numpy, grouped
    by layer idx. Manual safetensors parser (see _read_safetensors_file) — no torch dependency,
    CPU only, never touches the GPU."""
    st_files = sorted(model_dir.glob("*.safetensors"))
    if not st_files:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no safetensors in {model_dir}")

    o_proj = {}
    down_proj = {}
    layer_re = re.compile(r"\.layers\.(\d+)\.")
    for f in st_files:
        tensors = _read_safetensors_file(f)
        for key, arr in tensors.items():
            if "self_attn.o_proj.weight" in key:
                m = layer_re.search(key)
                if m:
                    o_proj[int(m.group(1))] = arr.astype(np.float32)
            elif "mlp.down_proj.weight" in key:
                m = layer_re.search(key)
                if m:
                    down_proj[int(m.group(1))] = arr.astype(np.float32)
    return o_proj, down_proj

Pour chaque couche on prend les **k plus petits** vecteurs singuliers gauches B_ℓ ∈ R^{d_model×k} (sous-espace de plus basse énergie de W_ℓ ; après ablation de k directions, il les contient). On cherche le sous-espace k-D le plus **partagé** via la somme des projecteurs M = Σ_ℓ B_ℓB_ℓᵀ : \\- alignment = (Σ des k plus grandes valeurs propres de M)/(n_layers·k) ∈ [~k/d_model, 1] : ≈1 si toutes les couches partagent le même sous-espace k-D (abliteré multi-dir), ~k/d_model si aléatoire (sain). \\- per_layer_align[ℓ] = ‖SᵀB_ℓ‖_F² / k ∈ [0,1] : fraction de l'énergie bas-k de la couche captée par le sous-espace partagé S (= k 1ers vec. propres de M) -> signal par couche pour la bande/heatmap. NB robustesse : le norm-preserving qui rescale les **colonnes** (d_in) préserve le noyau gauche -> bottom-k intact ; le rescale des **lignes** (d_model) le déplace -> signal atténué (c'est là que le plan comportemental prend le relais). k=1 redonne (au carré) le signal de `umin_signature`.\"\"\" n = handle.n_layers Bs = [] for l in range(n): U = _svd_left_U(handle.weight(target, l)) # [d_model, r] kk = min(k, U.shape[1]) Bs.append(U[:, -kk:]) # bottom-k gauche d = Bs[0].shape[0] M = np.zeros((d, d), dtype=np.float64) for B in Bs: M += B @ B.T # Σ projecteurs evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(M) # croissant S = evecs[:, ::-1][:, :k].astype(np.float32) # sous-espace partagé (top-k) alignment = float(evals[::-1][:k].sum() / (n * k)) if n > 0 else 0.0 per_layer = np.array( [float(np.sum((S.T @ B) ** 2) / B.shape[1]) for B in Bs], dtype=np.float32 ) return alignment, per_layer, S def weight_signatures(handle, target: WeightTarget, *, k: int = 4, progress=None): \"\"\"Signatures JORAK umin (k=1) ET sous-espace (bottom-k) en **une seule SVD par couche** (au lieu de deux passes séparées : ~2× moins de calcul sur un gros modèle), avec retour de progression par couche. Renvoie un dict : {align, pairwise, per_layer_align, Umat, # umin_signature sub_align, sub_per_layer, sub_shared}. # subspace_signature Résultats identiques à `umin_signature` + `subspace_signature` (mêmes maths) ; `progress(1, desc=...)` est appelé une fois par couche traitée -> la phase JORAK (longue et jusqu'ici muette) devient visible dans la barre.\"\"\" n = handle.n_layers us, Bs = [], [] for l in range(n): U = _svd_left_U(handle.weight(target, l)) # [d_model, r] — UNE SVD us.append(U[:, -1]) # u_min (bottom-1) kk = min(k, U.shape[1]) Bs.append(U[:, -kk:]) # bottom-k if progress is not None: progress(1, desc=f\"JORAK · weight layer {l + 1}/{n}\") # --- agrégat umin (cf. umin_signature) --- Umat = np.stack(us, axis=0).astype(np.float32) # [n_layers, d_model] _P, sv, Qh = np.linalg.svd(Umat, full_matrices=False) fro = float(np.linalg.norm(Umat)) align = float(sv[0] / fro) if fro > 0 else 0.0 shared = Qh[0] per_layer_align = np.abs(Umat @ shared).astype(np.float32) G = Umat @ Umat.T iu = np.triu_indices(Umat.shape[0], k=1) pairwise = float(np.mean(np.abs(G[iu]))) if iu[0].size else 0.0 # --- agrégat sous-espace (cf. subspace_signature) --- d = Bs[0].shape[0] M = np.zeros((d, d), dtype=np.float64) for B in Bs: M += B @ B.T evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(M) S = evecs[:, ::-1][:, :k].astype(np.float32) sub_align = float(evals[::-1][:k].sum() / (n * k)) if n > 0 else 0.0 sub_per_layer = np.array( [float(np.sum((S.T @ B) ** 2) / B.shape[1]) for B in Bs], dtype=np.float32 ) return { \"align\": align, \"pairwise\": pairwise, \"per_layer_align\": per_layer_align, \"Umat\": Umat, \"sub_align\": sub_align, \"sub_per_layer\": sub_per_layer, \"sub_shared\": S, } def _band_window(n_layers: int) -> int: \"\"\"Largeur de bande adaptée à la profondeur (≈ 1/6 des couches, min 3).\"\"\" return int(max(3, round(n_layers / 6))) def band_alignment(per_layer_align, window: int = None): \"\"\"Alignement de la BANDE la plus touchée -> (score, (début, fin)). L'alignement global ``σ₁/‖U‖_F`` moyenne platement sur toutes les couches et DILUE une ablation localisée (cas Heretic : seules ~4 couches touchées). On prend plutôt la **moyenne maximale sur une fenêtre de couches consécutives** (agnostique en position : la bande peut être au centre, en profondeur, …). As of August 2026: whether a model was abliterated is roughly solved. Which method is open. The components to build the missing classifier exist across three adjacent literatures; nobody has assembled them yet.\n\nUpdated August 30, 2026 · 14 min read · Edited by [Alexander von der Neymark](/about#editorial-team)\n\nQuick answer\n\nTwo 2026 preprints (Hurtado, arXiv:2607.01854; Messenger, IEEE Access 2026) can detect from internal signals whether a model was abliterated, at AUROC around 0.95. Messenger goes further and identifies four coarse mechanistic classes, distinguishing weight-orthogonalization abliteration from rotation-only abliteration, training-based removal, and behavioral fine-tuning. But no work outputs a specific M1-M9 label. The enabling technology exists in three literatures: weight-difference interpretability (WeightWatch, Diff Interpretation Tuning), model provenance and merge detection (MoTHer, GhostSpec, REEF, AttnDiff), and mechanistic diffing (crosscoders, LEACE). What is missing is a labeled dataset of (method, weights) pairs and a multi-class classifier over the M1-M9 taxonomy. Our catalog is precisely such a labeled dataset - that is the concrete opportunity.\n\nIn this article\n\n  * Why the current classifier depends entirely on what authors declare\n  * The two 2026 detectors that can identify abliteration without asking the author (Hurtado two-signal audit, Messenger AMS)\n  * Why detecting removal is easier than detecting method - and what the specific separations we can already see are\n  * The three adjacent literatures whose components would compose into a method fingerprinter\n  * What would be needed to build a Method Fingerprinting Benchmark: labeled data, weights-only operation, hard negatives, robustness testing\n  * Why the catalog is uniquely positioned to be that labeled dataset\n  * What thresholds would change these recommendations\n\n\n\n## The question this article maps\n\nEvery model in the catalog carries an editorial method label: M1, M3, M8+M1, and so on. That label is computed from what the author declared: name, tags, yaml metadata, file structure. See [how we label the method for each model](/wiki/methodology-of-method-labeling/) for the twelve rules. The label is transparent by construction, revisable, and honest about its origin. But it starts from what the author said. If we had a candidate model and knew nothing about who produced it or how, could we look at the weights and decide \"this is M1\" or \"this is M3 followed by M8\"?\n\nThat is the question this article surveys. The short answer, as of August 2026, is: partially. Whether a model has been abliterated at all can now be detected from internal signals with AUROC around 0.95. Whether the removal was single-direction (Arditi-style, M1) or per-layer (Heretic, M3 with M1 secondary) is beginning to be distinguishable. Whether an abliteration was followed by DPO healing (M4) versus left raw is not directly tested by any existing work. Whether two abliterated models were merged (M5-frankenstein territory) is the most tractable sub-question because merge attribution is a mature sub-field. Nobody has yet built a multi-class classifier that outputs an M1-M9 label directly.\n\nThe components to build it exist. The gap is real. The catalog is uniquely positioned as the labeled training data. This article maps the terrain.\n\n## The \"whether\" question is roughly solved\n\nTwo independent groups published, both in 2026, methods that detect from internal signals whether refusal has been removed from a checkpoint, without any dependence on what the author claimed.\n\n### Hurtado, two-signal audit (Moonsong Labs)\n\n**Has This Checkpoint Been Abliterated? A Two-Signal Audit and Its Failure Map.** Gabriel Hurtado, [arXiv:2607.01854](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01854) v2 (August 2026). Combines two cheap internal signals into a threshold-free audit:\n\n  1. **Reference-anchored activation refusal-gap ratio** : given a candidate model and a trusted base, measures the activation-space gap at the last token between refused and complied outputs. The ratio is near 1 for an intact model and falls toward 0 as refusal is removed.\n  2. **Weight-recovery energy** : the rank-1 energy fraction of the base-to-candidate weight difference (borrowed conceptually from WeightWatch). Different removal recipes leave different rank profiles in the weight diff.\n\n\n\nOn a 273-checkpoint registry spanning Qwen, DeepSeek-distilled Qwen, Llama, and Gemma, the combined z-sum score separates 57 public abliterations from 37 benign fine-tunes, merges, and instruction-tunes at in-sample AUROC 0.95, above either signal alone (weight energy 0.90, activation gap 0.84). Under leave-one-family-out transfer, single-signal AUROCs drop to 0.81 and 0.78 respectively, while the combined score reaches balanced accuracy around 0.89 (false positive rate 0.11) and detects 53 of 57 uncensored checkpoints. The four misses are described as ordinary abliteration variants rather than the harder recipes.\n\n**What this means for us** : the \"whether refusal was removed\" question is functionally answered for practical triage. Not for tamper-proofing (see failures below), but for surveying the catalog it is now possible to independently verify author declarations at scale.\n\n### Messenger, AMS activation scanner (Google)\n\n**Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis.** G. Messenger, [arXiv:2608.05578](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05578), IEEE Access vol. 14 pp. 91723-91737 (2026). Introduces AMS (Activation-based Model Scanner), which measures the geometric separation between harmful and benign content clusters in the activation space of a candidate model. Its central contribution for our purposes is not just detection but a four-class mechanistic taxonomy of what different removal recipes look like at the activation level:\n\ni · training removal\n\nCluster separation collapses. Direction is not preserved. Signature seen in base models and Dolphin variants; sigma range 0.5 to 1.4.\n\nii · weight-orthogonalization abliteration\n\nSeparation collapses AND the refusal direction is rotated. Signature seen in Llama-3.1-abliterated: sigma 3.33, direction cosine 0.30.\n\niii · rotation-without-collapse abliteration\n\nSeparation preserved but direction rotated.
